newsitem.title: UK: ING works on plans for Dalgety bid-Telegraph.
newsitem.headline: ING works on plans for Dalgety bid-Telegraph.

text.p: Investment bank ING Barings is working on plans for a 900 million pound break-up bid of British petfoods and agricultural feeds firm Dalgety Plc, the Sunday Telegraph reported.

The Telegraph said the bank had approached a series of the world's largest food groups -- including Nestle SA in Switzerland, Ralston Purina Co of the U.S., and Associated British Foods -- to see if they would be interested in bidding for all parts of the business.
ING Barings was not immediately available for comment on Sunday.
The Telegraph said Barings had been working on the plans since Dalgety issued a profits warning in July.
The paper said while other investment banks are also said to have looked at organising a bid for Dalgety, Barings plans were by far the most advanced and well thought out.
Under the terms of the proposed deal, one of the companies would bid for Dalgety and could then recoup a large proportion of the cost by selling off the unwanted operations.
